title: Hot-swap a server's failed power supply without disturbing the live one
instruction: The power supply with the amber light has failed. Replace it with the spare power supply on the table, without disturbing the power supply with the green light, which is keeping the server running.
context: Data-center technicians replace failed redundant (N+1) server power supplies while the server keeps running on the other one: the latch has to be released by the hand that pulls, and the long, heavy new unit pushed in square until its latch catches, without knocking the live unit.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Power-supply cage: grey sheet steel (or PLA), fixed to the table, two bays side by side facing the arms with their mouths at x 36.95, each 7.75 cm wide, 4.05 cm tall under a 0.4 cm roof and 18.45 cm deep from the mouth to a back stop, separated by a 1.5 cm divider; the left bay is centred on y 0 and the right on y -9.25. Each side wall has a 1.5 cm lead-in plate at the mouth, flared 30 degrees. The server body continues 13.1 cm behind the back stop. In the left wall of each bay, 0.9 to 2.65 cm inside the mouth and 1.3 to 2.7 cm above the table, is a 1.75 x 1.4 cm notch. At the back of each bay a spring plunger (edge-connector stand-in, 3 N per mm) acts over the last 1.4 mm of insertion. Three identical CRPS power supplies, black, 18.5 x 7.35 x 3.95 cm, 0.9 kg. Each has an orange vertical grip handle (1 x 0.8 x 4.8 cm) on its centreline, standing 2.75 cm in front of its face on two thin guide arms; the handle and a hook on the supply's left side are one 60 g part that slides 0.5 cm sideways (spring 0.3 N per mm). At rest the hook's square catch (0.4 x 0.5 x 1.2 cm, 1.25 cm behind the face) stands 0.5 cm out of the side into the bay wall's notch; behind it a 1 cm ramp slopes back to the side at 27 degrees. Pushing the handle 0.5 cm to the right draws the hook in. The failed supply (amber light) is latched in the left bay and the live supply (green light) in the right bay, each face 0.2 cm proud of its mouth; the spare (no light) lies on the table with its centre at x 23.5, y 22, face toward the arms.
scoring: Measured with a ruler and a top photo; positions from where a supply sits latched home in the left bay. 0 if the live (green) supply was at any point moved more than 5 mm. Otherwise: 1.0 if the spare is home in the left bay (within 1.5 mm along it and 2 mm across it, level within 3 degrees) with its hook out in the notch (handle within 1 mm of its rest position), the failed supply is clear of the bay (back face at least 5 mm in front of the mouth, or its centre more than 7.85 cm to the side), and the spare is still (moving less than 1 mm over 1 s), for 1 s; 0.75 if, after the failed supply came out, the spare was pushed in with its back face 10 cm inside the mouth; 0.5 if the failed supply was pulled all the way out (back face 5 mm in front of the mouth); 0.25 if it was pulled at least 2 cm out; else 0.
reset_notes: Push the failed supply back into the left bay until its hook snaps into the notch; put the spare back on its marked outline. The live supply is not moved.
fidelity: Rigid boxes; supplies are full CRPS size and weight. The latch is one sprung slider: the real CRPS tab and fixed handle are merged, so the handle itself slides aside; the hook has a real square catch and ramp. The handle is enlarged (2.75 cm proud, 4.8 cm tall) for gripper fingers. The connector is a 4.2 N spring plunger, lighter than real (the arms can't push more). Bays have 2 mm clearance a side. The cage is fixed; no power cords (taken as unplugged). Light angular damping.
